items.title: Take a Look at A24 Music’s Custom Audio-Technica Sound Burger
items.summary:
Summary 

A24 Music and Audio-Technica launch a limited-edition Sound Burger portable turntable.The Bluetooth-enabled AT-SB727 features a custom red, blue, and green colorway.Priced at $270 USD, the 1,000-unit drop hits A24’s webstore.

A24 Music has officially teamed up with Audio-Technica to introduce the Sound Burger A24 Music Edition. Serving as a limited-edition iteration of the AT-SB727 portable turntable, the collaborative release breathes new life into a historic piece of audio tech. Originally introduced to the market in 1982, the Sound Burger is celebrated for its highly unique, compact design that allows vinyl records to spin outside of the main body, enabling users to play physical media without the need for a full stereo setup.

Aesthetically, the A24 Music Edition updates the retro turntable with a striking, signature red, blue, and green colorway. The highly portable device features an exclusive panel stamped with an original A24 Music logo design, alongside a special emblem plate to mark the partnership.

In terms of technical specs, the internal AT-SB727 mechanism supports both 33-1/3 and 45 RPM records and boasts a USB-C rechargeable battery that delivers approximately 12 hours of playback. Embracing modern connectivity, the device seamlessly streams audio to wireless speakers and headphones via Bluetooth 5.2, while also providing a traditional RCA cable for wired home setups.

Priced at $270 USD with only 1,000 units produced, the Sound Burger A24 Music Edition is sold exclusively through A24’s website and only in North America. Pre-orders are now open…
items.t: Take a Look at A24 Music’s Custom Audio-Technica Sound Burger

items.title: 12_Things Rejects The Conventions of Perfumery
items.summary:
'Challenging' isn't a word you'd normally use when describing perfumes and colognes, but its a term that's become somewhat of an inspiration for a new fragrance brand named 12_Things. 

Founded in London by Charlie Vickery, the brand has been built around a "rejection of conventional perfume language", resulting in notes taken from unexpected sources. Throughout the initial collection of eight fragrances, Vickery explores modern life, particularly one spent in the city. Rather than your typical rose, vanilla, or musk, he opts for a combination of skin, salt, asphalt, oxygen, plastic, metal, ink, dust and air. Even the names themselves are intentionally evocative – some more literal than others: Inkskin; White Dust; Infrastructure; Condensation; Vacuum; Interference; Cold Storage; and Void. 

"The smells that stay with me are often the ones nobody would put in an advert," Vickery says. "A hospital corridor can hold an entire period of your life. The smell of rain lifting off asphalt can tell you where you belong. I wanted to give those experiences the care normally reserved for more beautiful subjects."

Every detail, from the bottle, through to the store itself, is the brainchild of Vickery. "The physical experience matters as much as the image on a screen," he says. 

Conceptually, Vickery also wants clients to think about the end of the brand – which may seem like a funny idea, considering it's only just launched. This particularly manifests in the physical store itself, which gradually deconstructs as each perfume is bought. 

Inside the London space, located at 198…
items.t: 12_Things Rejects The Conventions of Perfumery

items.title: A Night Out in NYC with Xaviersobased and PUMA
items.summary:
A party for the new Hypebeast Magazine issue with Xaviersobased and his hometown crowd — what better way to spend a Friday the 13th? Last week, we celebrated the launch of The Juice Issue with the cover star in New York City, and between the pop-up signing and live performance, the energy never let up.

First stop was Iconic Magazines & Cafe, a perennial Nolita favorite. Fans started wrapping the building hours before Xav pulled up, and by the time he arrived, donning his signature green hair and a new pair of earrings he copped for the occasion, the street was packed. From behind the cafe's counter, he signed copies for a few hours, took photos with fans, and even gave away free copies. Of course, his mom and aunt showed up to show some love.

Afterwards, Xavier and the crowd moved the night to lounge one4one just a short walk away. The floor filled quickly as DJs Nurse and Rennessy set the tone before the rapper took the mic for a performance of his own. The setlist included songs from his self-titled album, like "Room service" and "Party at my place," before moving into the earlier "Softer" and unreleased "Wassup W It." Sporting classic PUMA Suedes , that he eventually tossed into the crowd, he kept the momentum up as fans and friends packed in close.

This year has been a big one for the under-turned-overground rap star — a debut album, a world tour with Ken Carson, another of his own, all with Coachella 2027 on the horizon — and there's no signs of slowing down. His stage is only growing, but as the night proved, keeping his people close as always part of the plan.…
items.t: A Night Out in NYC with Xaviersobased and PUMA

items.title: A Look Back at Maison Martell’s Creative Exchange in Chanteloup
items.summary:
Maison Martell invited four fashion visionaries to Château de Chanteloup earlier this fall. Serving as the base for a unique creative exchange, the historic estate, which the Cognac Maison has called home for decades, inspired discussions on heritage, craft, and, more importantly, future collaborations.

The collective in attendance included Johannesburg-based multidisciplinary artist Rich Mnisi and Nigerian-American designer and image director Ugo Mozie , as well as New York-based designers Brandon Blackwood and Jacques Agbobly . Hailing from different areas of fashion, the experience aimed to bring them together under a shared mission of discovery, where they would find out what shapes their creative worlds.

Before delving further into their own practices, the appointed “Swift Ones” explored the journey behind Martell’s cognacs, from the vineyard through to distillation, barrel-making and ageing. The group later took part in a blending experience, where they created their individual blends. The immersion also included the Signature Martell dinner at Château de Chanteloup, providing a gastronomic experience by three-Michelin-starred chef Alexandre Mazzia.

The collective then joined heads for a group conversation led by Martell Culture Ambassador Ivie Ani. With the tour bringing heritage into perspective, they spoke about the stories that form their journeys. Reflecting on this, Mozie shared, “Every final expression is built through layers, people, process, material, time, and instinct. That is very similar to how I approach designing and styling; what you eventually see…
items.t: A Look Back at Maison Martell’s Creative Exchange in Chanteloup

items.title: Noah and Converse Take the Chuck 70 Back to the ’90s in Black Watch Tartan
items.summary:
Name: Noah x Converse Chuck 70 Tartan
 Colorway: TBC
 SKU: TBC
 MSRP: TBC
 Release Date: November 19
 Where to Buy: Converse , Noah 

Converse and Noah have teamed up on a new Chuck 70 Ox in Black Watch tartan, the navy and green check that began in the Scottish Highlands roughly 300 years ago and later became a mainstay of collegiate style. The pair keeps the focus on its materials and construction, giving the traditional plaid a Chuck 70 built to ’90s specs.

The upper does most of the work. It is made from a three-tone woven canvas with the Black Watch plaid running across the whole shoe, so the pattern comes from the weave itself rather than a surface print. That gives the check a richer, more textured look than a printed plaid, and it suits the cold-weather timing of the release.

Noah based the shoe’s build on Chucks from the ’90s. The brand removed the wing tongue stitch seen on the current Chuck 70 and swapped in a woven tongue tag, so the profile reads closer to how the shoe looked in that decade. The upper sits on a light brown gum rubber outsole, which warms up the navy and green and adds to the vintage feel.

Inside, an OrthoLite sockliner adds cushioning for everyday wear. Noah keeps its branding minimal, placing it on the heel license plate, the tongue tag and the insole and leaving the tartan to carry the design. The release follows the two brands’ Spring 2026 Chuck 70 capsule, which first brought plaid into the partnership .

items.title: Lamborghini Proves There Doesn’t Need To Be a Compromise With the Temerario Spyder
items.summary:
Summary 

Lamborghini unveils the Temerario Spyder, featuring its first-ever fully electric retractable hard top.Featuring a 907-horsepower twin-turbo V8 hybrid powertrain catapults the supercar from 0 to 62 mph in 2.8 seconds.An enlarged cabin and 13 driving modes ensure uncompromised comfort and performance.

Lamborghini has officially unveiled the Temerario Spyder, marking 50 years of open-top series-production with another bold engineering milestone. A first for any Lamborghini Spyder, the supercar features a fully electric retractable hard top.

Rather than relying on traditional hydraulics, the roof utilizes ten electric actuators to tuck vertically behind the seats. This packaging preserves the car’s weight distribution while lowering its center of gravity by three mm when stowed. The entire mechanism operates at near silence, taking 17 seconds to go up or down at speed of up to 31 mph. 

Underneath, torsional rigidity has been increased by six percent over its predecessor while reducing structural complexity. Power comes from a HPEV setup, mating its flat-plane 4.0 liter twin-turbo V8 with three electric motors. Revving to a screaming 10,000 rpm, the hybrid powertrain churns out a combined 907 horsepower and 590 pound-feet of torque, catapulting the car from 0-to-62 in just 2.8 seconds.

Inside, the enlarged cabin gains space over its predecessor, comfortably fitting drivers up to two meters tall, complete with integrated neck warmers and an electronically adjustable rear window that lets occupants listen to the V8 sing. With 13 selectable driving modes, including…
items.t: Lamborghini Proves There Doesn’t Need To Be a Compromise With the Temerario Spyder

While the event serves as artistic director Demna ’s first show in the city, Gucci is no stranger to the Chinese metropolis. The heritage brand previously hosted runway presentations in Shanghai for its Fall 2012 collection under Frida Giannini and its centenary Aria collection by Alessandro Michele in 2021. The label has also maintained a strong cultural footprint in the region through various high-profile exhibitions, including 2015's "No Longer / Not Yet," the Maurizio Cattelan-curated "The Artist Is Present" in 2018, "Gucci Cosmos" in 2023, and "Gucci Bamboo: Decoding an Icon" in 2025.

The Shanghai announcement follows Demna's massive debut Cruise collection for the house, which took over New York City's Times Square last May. Tied directly to the iconic tournament at Augusta National, the forthcoming release serves as the latest addition to the brand's rapidly growing golf lineup, seamlessly transitioning familiar basketball models onto the fairway.

Keeping the timeless look of the original basketball shoe intact, the new iteration arrives with a crisp white leather upper paired with a striking green patent leather mudguard. The carefully chosen shade of green perfectly mirrors the distinct color closely associated with Augusta National and the prestigious Masters Tournament.

On the performance side, the silhouette has been heavily modified for the green. Underneath, the low-top sneaker rests on a green-to-silver gradient plate that features seven strategically placed circular spikes to ensure premium traction throughout the golf course.

The Air Jordan 11 Low Golf "The Masters" drops in April 2027. Official pricing and retail channels remain TBA.

items.title: Maserati Celebrates a Century of their Legendary Trident at AutoClassica 2026
items.summary:
Summary 

Maserati celebrates 100 years of its Trident emblem at Milano AutoClassica 2026.A rare 1959 3500 GT Convertible Vignale Prototype is displayed alongside the new 490-hp GranCabrio.Historic motorsport icons also headline the showcase from November 19 to 22. 

Maserati is celebrating a century of its legendary Trident emblem by placing two of its iconic grand tourers side-by-side at Milano Auto Classica 2026. The showcase puts the ultra-rare 1959 Maserati 3500 GT Convertible Vignale Prototype next to the modern Maserati GranCabrio .

Built in Modena and unveiled at the 1959 Turin Motor Show, the 3500 GT Convertible Vignale Prototype is one of just six units ever produced. Designed by Carrozzeria Alfredo Vignale under Giovanni Michelotti, the drop-top established the blueprint for Maserati’s modern convertible grand tourers. Having been meticulously restored over the past three years, the silver-bodied classic retains its original 235-hp, 3.5-liter inline-six engine and a striking ivory, red, and gold interior inspired by the Vignale emblem.

Placed beside its predecessor, the contemporary Maserati GranCabrio demonstrates the evolution of their design language. Finished in Blu Emozione over a Greige leather and carbon-fiber cabin, the latest iteration features a redesigned front end for improved downforce and a wider track. Under the hood, Maserati’s F1-derived 3.0-liter Twin Turbo V6 delivers 490 hp alongside a new Country driving mode.

Beyond the main booth, attendees can explore Maserati’s lineage in the main hall, with motorsport icons 6C34, the Tipo 61, and the…

On the performance side, the collection reinterprets martial arts staples through Affliction’s rebellious lens. The lineup features a co-branded Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu gi heavily accented with detailed embroidery and flame-tribal insignias. An expansive no-gi offering includes rashguards and training shorts bearing all-over cross-monogram prints and gothic co-branding, while a technical wrestling polo anchors the training assortment in functional athletic tailoring with branded collar details.

Off the mats, the lifestyle selection translates that same raw energy into casual apparel. The range includes relaxed-fit washed denim detailed with oversized back-pocket graphics, layered long-sleeves, heavy hoodies, and sweatpants. items.title: Bottega Veneta Looks Homeward for Spring 2027 With "Colours of Venice"
items.summary:
Summary 

Bottega Veneta unveils "Colours of Venice," a Spring 2027 photo series shot by Chris Rhodes.Under Creative Director Louise Trotter, the imagery pairs saturated hues with historic Venetian interiors.Accessories spotlight the iconic Cabat tote and the new, 1970s-inspired Verde handbag.

Returning to its roots in the Veneto region, Bottega Veneta didn’t settle for just a tourist’s-eye view of the city. For Spring 2027 , Creative Director Louise Trotter once again taps British photographer Chris Rhodes to lens “Colours of Venice,” a photo series that focuses on tactile, live-in study of light and surface instead of grand canal panoramas.

Rather than treating the city as a static backdrop, Rhodes weaves between intimate interiors and open streets. Pink-plastered walls, intricate terrazzo flooring, rich damask fabrics, and gilded mirrors add textural depth to the clothing. Held close to the surroundings, the garments’ construction and saturated tones are highlighted through the use of natural light, creating a visual dialogue between Venice’s weathered surfaces and Trotter’s contemporary tailoring.

Leather goods remain the anchor of the seasonal narrative. Alongside the signature Cabat tote, Spring 2027 introduces the Verde, a new handbag that channels the laid-back ease of 1970s designs into a compact, architectural silhouette. Finished with engraved gold-toned hardware, the Verde features a soft leather flap that lifts to reveal Bottega Veneta’s signature Intrecciato weave tucked underneath.

Rooted in Bottega Veneta’s Venetian roots, “Colours of Venice” focuses on…
items.t: Bottega Veneta Looks Homeward for Spring 2027 With "Colours of Venice"

items.title: Oris and Doraemon Travel Through Time on a Big Crown Pointer Date Watch
items.summary:
Summary 

Oris reimagines its Big Crown Pointer Date with Japanese manga icon Doraemon.A light blue dial, red minute track and yellow hands mirror the character.A flying Doraemon caseback engraving marks the 1,000-piece edition.

Oris is teaming up with one of Japan’s best-loved characters for its latest limited edition. The Swiss brand has released a Doraemon version of its signature Big Crown Pointer Date, inspired by the original manga by Fujiko F. Fujio, first published in 1970.

Conceived around a shared fascination with mechanics and time travel, the timepiece channels the cheerful aesthetic of the 22nd-century robotic cat into a wearable, subtle design. The idea came from Jo Haertel Yamaguchi, Sales Manager of Oris Japan, who drew inspiration from the brand’s earlier Kermit the Frog edition and grew up reading the manga in the 1980s. “I don’t think we’ve ever seen a Doraemon watch as charming as this,” he said in an interview included with the release.

The design keeps the references subtle. Housed in a 40mm multi-piece stainless steel case, this special timepiece features a vertically brushed light blue dial that matches Doraemon’s body color, while the red minute track picks up the color of his signature collar. The central seconds hand and the tip of the pointer date hand are yellow, a nod to the HOPTER, the propeller gadget Doraemon pulls from his 4D pocket so he can fly.

Flipping the watch over reveals a caseback engraved with Doraemon in flight, a fitting touch given the Big Crown’s aviation roots, along with each watch’s limited-edition number. The fun…

items.title: The 14 best men’s boots for winter, from chelseas and lace-ups to wellies
items.summary:
Whether you want minimalist or heritage, waterproof or suede, our menswear expert has rounded up the most stylish pairs for every occasion and outfit

• The best men’s coats for autumn and winter

I haven’t always worn boots. For years I wrote them off – at 5ft 8in, I was convinced anything above the ankle would make my legs look shorter. Then I started wearing them with the right trousers – a straight leg that falls over the top – and realised I’d spent a decade getting winter wrong. All anyone sees is a smart pair of shoes that happens to keep your ankles warm.

Here’s the thing: boots needn’t be intimidating. They’re just the wintry version of the leather shoes you already own. A chelsea is your loafer – it goes with pretty much everything in your wardrobe and every event in your diary, Christmas parties included. A derby boot is laced up, a bit sturdier and just as happy with jeans. The chukka is your weekend trainer. And the chunky, rubber-soled ones? Just think of them as an umbrella for your feet.
